# firstboot_domain (Resource)

A domain registration.

**This resource buys something, and `terraform destroy` cannot sell it back.** A registry does not take a name back and the money is spent when the order is accepted, so destroying this resource only makes Terraform FORGET the domain: it stays registered, and it keeps renewing if `auto_renew` is on. Guard it:

```hcl
resource "firstboot_domain" "example" {
  name       = "example.com"
  years      = 1
  contact_id = firstboot_domain_contact.main.id

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
```

The registrant contact has to exist before the order. There is no `firstboot_domain_contact` resource yet -- create the profile in the panel and pass its id.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `contact_id` (String) The registrant profile the name is registered to. Create it in the panel first.

**Cannot be changed here.** Moving a registration to another registrant is a registry operation with its own rules and its own transfer lock; the API offers no endpoint for it.
- `name` (String) The full name including the extension, e.g. `example.com`.

**Cannot be changed.** A different name is a different registration, and editing this in place would mean abandoning a name that is still paid for and still renewing. Remove the resource block and write a new one.
- `years` (Number) The registration term, 1 to 10. Charged upfront from the wallet.

**Cannot be changed.** Extending a registration is a RENEWAL, which is a second purchase rather than an edit, and this provider does not spend money from a plan that reads like a settings change. Renew from the panel.

### Optional

- `auto_renew` (Boolean) Whether the registration renews itself before expiry. Changed in place.

Turning it OFF is how a domain is allowed to lapse; there is no other way, because nothing here can withdraw a registration.
- `nameservers` (List of String) Two to thirteen hostnames to delegate the zone to. Changed in place.

This is what you ASKED for; `nameservers_applied` is what the registrar has confirmed. They differ while a change is in flight, and a change that never lands stays visible as the difference between the two rather than silently reading back as applied.
- `privacy` (Boolean) WHOIS privacy, where the registry offers it. Changed in place.
- `project_id` (String) Optional project to group the domain under. Changing it moves the domain in place; it is not a replacement.
- `registrar_lock` (Boolean) The registrar's transfer lock. Changed in place.

Leaving it on is the cheapest anti-hijack control a domain has; it has to come off only to transfer the name away.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags on this domain, used to select it from a `firstboot_*` data source and to filter it in the panel.

At most 10, each up to 32 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `:` and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit. `env:prod` is a convention, not a schema: a tag is one flat string.

**Written exactly as given.** The API stores tags lowercased, so a tag that is not already lowercase is refused at plan time rather than silently rewritten — a rewritten value would differ from the configuration on every subsequent plan.
- `wait_for_active` (Boolean) Whether apply waits for the registry to confirm the order. With it off, the resource exists in state while the name may still be refused -- and a refusal is refunded, so the difference shows up as a domain that never became `active`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `dns_zone_id` (String) The DNS zone created for this name, when the platform's own nameservers are the ones serving it.
- `expires_at` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `last_error_code` (String) The registry's own refusal code, when there was one.
- `nameservers_applied` (List of String) What the registrar last CONFIRMED, as opposed to what was asked for.
- `registered_at` (String)
- `state` (String) `active`, `expired`, `redemption` and `failed` are settled; `registering` and `transfer_pending` mean the registry has not answered yet. A `failed` order is refunded in full.
- `tld` (String)
- `transferable_at` (String) When the registry's 60-day post-registration transfer lock lifts. It is enforced by the registry, not by this platform.
